sections.h2: Who sends the Oldham County tax bill
sections.html:
Oldham County's sheriff mails and collects the bill, while the Property Valuation Administration (PVA) sets the value behind it. One bill rolls together what is owed to the state, the county, the school districts, Crestwood and 18 special districts. Envelopes are in the mail by the end of September, and the sheriff's number is 502-222-9501.

The sheriff's site also has a Property Tax FAQ that goes into payment options. Anything about a value that looks wrong goes to the PVA at 502-222-9320, because the sheriff never assigns value to a parcel. The bill itself shows the due dates, how to avoid penalties and what a mortgage servicer's payment looks like.

Oldham County sits in north central Kentucky and is part of the Louisville metro area, with the Ohio River forming its northern edge against Indiana. La Grange is the seat and the biggest city. Crestwood, Goshen, Pewee Valley, Prospect, Orchard Grass Hills and River Bluff are cities too, and Buckner and Westport are census-designated places. Prospect lies mostly in Jefferson County, so confirm which county bills a Prospect parcel.

Prices run well above the state norm, and the county keeps growing: it gained roughly 3,400 residents between April 2020 and July 2025.

  • Population is 70,986 for 2025, up 5.0 percent since April 2020.
  • A typical owned home is worth $393,100, and owners live in 87.1 percent of occupied homes.
  • Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $2,193 a month. Those without one pay $712.
  • Rent runs $1,219 a month at the median, and household income is $122,497.
  • The county has 24,896 housing units, and builders pulled 276 permits in 2025.

School zones drive many buyer questions. The county is served by North Oldham, Oldham County and South Oldham high schools, so know which one serves your address.

Oldham County follows the statewide calendar in KRS 134.015.

Oldham County payment calendar

  • With escrow, verify the lender paid ahead of the discount deadline.
  • For a fall closing, get the title agent to say who pays the current bill.
  • In Crestwood, the city levy shows up on the sheriff's bill.

The owner on January 1 owes that year's tax, so a spring seller still gets the bill and splits it with the buyer at the closing table.

sections.h2: What to do about a high valuation
sections.html:
The first step is a conference with the PVA. Bring your own number and backing for it, such as nearby sales, a recent appraisal, contractor quotes or rent records. A statewide PVA appeal guide lays out the whole path.

If talks fail, the route runs through the Oldham County Clerk to a three-resident local board and finally to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, where the deadline is 30 days from the mailed ruling. In a county with prices this high, sales from the same subdivision make the strongest evidence.

sections.h2: Getting ready for a PVA conference
sections.html:
A conference goes better when you walk in with paper. Collect a few items before you call 502-222-9320: your latest bill, any recent appraisal, photos of defects such as a worn roof or foundation cracks, quotes from contractors, and sale prices for three or four houses near yours. For a rental, add rent and expense records.

Write down the value you think is right and why. A figure with backing behind it is far harder to wave off than a complaint that the number feels high. If the PVA does not budge, you will still have a record to carry to the local board.

Keep paying the bill while the appeal runs, because a higher final value later produces a supplemental charge.

sections.h2: Where unpaid Oldham County bills end up
sections.html:
Anything the sheriff has not collected by closing time on April 15 goes to the County Clerk. The clerk's delinquent tax page sends value disputes to the PVA and sale questions to the Department of Revenue.

From there the parcel is liened, interest runs at 1 percent monthly, the county attorney mails warnings, and a sale waits at least 90 days after the transfer. If an investor buys the certificate, the owner then owes the investor.

If you are selling, get the clerk's written quote and settle it from your proceeds at closing. The title company will ask for it anyway.

sections.h2: Charges at closing for an Oldham County seller
sections.html:
Kentucky's transfer tax is the seller's: fifty cents for each $500 of value, counting any remainder as a full $500, taken by the clerk with the deed (KRS 142.050). Deeds between spouses, corrective deeds and foreclosure deeds are exempt.

  • Every deed lists the full price, mailing addresses for both sides and a forwarding address for the next tax bill.
  • A gift or token-price sale needs a sworn market-value estimate.
  • Heirs file the personal representative's affidavit wherever the estate holds land.

sections.h2: Why bills differ from street to street
sections.html:
The sheriff bills 18 special districts and one city, so neighbors a few miles apart can owe different totals. Before you compare listings, check which districts appear on each bill.

When you set an asking price, use a recent bill for your own address and expect a buyer to do the same. Ask the sheriff or the PVA if anything on it looks unfamiliar.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with a tax problem
sections.html:
A house with a lien on it can still be sold. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds. If you want a quicker route than a traditional listing, a cash sale skips the lender's appraisal and the buyer's financing wait, and the lien still gets paid at closing.

  1. Call the clerk for a written payoff and ask how long it stays good.
  2. Confirm that the current year's bill is paid or prorated.
  3. Ask the sheriff to confirm nothing is open from earlier years.
  4. Bring the payoff and receipts to the title company before the closing date.

sections.h2: Escrow, servicers and the January 1 rule
sections.html:
Many owners never write a check, because a mortgage servicer pays from escrow. That is fine until a sale or a refinance, when the paid-through date matters. Ask the servicer for a statement showing what it paid and when, and make sure the discount deadline was met if you want the 2 percent saving.

Ownership on January 1 decides who is billed for the year. A seller who closes after that date will still see the sheriff's envelope with their name on it, and the title agent will prorate the total between the two sides. Put the split in writing, hand the agent your copy of the bill and keep the receipt for your own tax records.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about an Oldham County valuation?
faqs.a: The PVA, 502-222-9320. Values come from that office, and the sheriff only collects what they produce.

faqs.q: When do Oldham County property tax bills arrive?
faqs.a: Mailing wraps up by the end of September. Call the sheriff at 502-222-9501 if yours is missing in early October.

faqs.q: Is Crestwood's city tax billed separately?
faqs.a: No. The Crestwood levy rides on the same sheriff bill as the county and district charges, so a single payment covers all of them.

faqs.q: Who pays the transfer tax on an Oldham County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, at fifty cents per $500 of value, paid to the clerk before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can a house with a tax lien on it still be sold in Oldham County?
faqs.a: Yes. The County Clerk quotes a payoff valid through a stated date, and the title company pays it from the sale proceeds.
